title: Depression and Anxiety Screening in Primary Care

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult in primary care or the emergency room with low mood, worry, panic or unexplained physical symptoms: screening with the PHQ-2, PHQ-9 and GAD-7, immediate suicide-risk action, severity-based treatment (psychological, medicine, or both), antidepressant and anxiolytic choices with doses, review timings, referral to psychiatry and relapse prevention, using the Saudi Ministry of Health (MOH) major depressive disorder and anxiety disorders protocols. Scoring cut-offs, starting-dose gaps and safety cautions are filled from named international sources and labelled. Children, adolescents, bipolar disorder, psychosis and peripartum depression are outside this topic. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

Medicine list restructured into a branched decision pathway on 2026-10-18. Doses, routes, adjustments, monitoring, contraindications and sources are unchanged from authoring-standard-2026-10-18-saudi3-v1-live.
unverifiedSections: The MOH major depressive disorder protocol lists the PHQ-9 and the MOH anxiety protocol lists the GAD-7 without scoring cut-offs; the cut-offs shown (PHQ-9 bands, PHQ-2 score of 3, GAD-7 cut-points 5, 10 and 15) come from the PHQ scoring summary and the GAD-7 scoring instructions and are not MOH statements.

The MOH protocols give usual dose ranges only; they do not give starting doses, titration steps or maximum daily doses beyond the top of the range. Apart from the MOH anxiety statement to start at half the usual starting dose, the starting dose must come from the product information or hospital formulary.

Neither MOH protocol gives suicide-risk assessment, a safety or crisis plan, contraindications, drug interactions, renal or hepatic adjustment, pregnancy or breastfeeding guidance, discontinuation guidance, or explicit psychiatry referral criteria. The immediate safety actions shown for a positive suicide question are standard clinical practice added here, not a quoted MOH statement, and need local review.

The PHQ scoring summary does not say how item 9 (thoughts of being better off dead or of self-harm) is handled; the same-day risk assessment rule is added as clinical practice and is not from that source.

The MOH depressive disorder protocol does not list sertraline, citalopram or paroxetine with doses; sertraline appears here only through NHS usage advice (once daily, low start, increase after a week or more) without milligram doses, which were not available.
The NHS fluoxetine page could not be read; fluoxetine doses are the MOH ranges (20 to 60 mg for depression, 20 to 80 mg for anxiety) with no other fluoxetine guidance.
Esketamine, electroconvulsive therapy, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and augmentation agents are summarised from the MOH protocol for completeness; specialist (psychiatry) use only.
The MOH anxiety protocol prints its propranolol dose as 40 mg every 8 to 12 hours in generalised anxiety disorder and 10 to 120 mg a day in social anxiety disorder; both are shown as printed.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.

Medicine pathway: branch entry criteria, preferred options and “use when” conditions were assigned from this topic's own indications and management steps. Confirm each against the cited guideline before clinical use.

pathophysiology.summary: Major depressive disorder is diagnosed by DSM-5 criteria: low mood or loss of interest for at least two weeks with other symptoms (sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, guilt, psychomotor change and recurrent thoughts of death), with functional impairment (MOH). The MOH depressive disorder protocol splits care into two tiers: mild disease (non-drug options) versus moderate to severe (medicine plus psychological treatment). The MOH anxiety protocol covers generalised anxiety disorder, panic disorder and social anxiety disorder; initial choice is by severity (mild to moderate: cognitive behavioural therapy, medicine or both; severe: both). Medical causes (for example hyperthyroidism), substances (for example caffeine) and comorbid conditions must be excluded before diagnosing an anxiety disorder (MOH). Women have a higher lifetime prevalence of major depressive disorder in Saudi Arabia than men (MOH).

references.edition: PHQ scoring summary, Table PHQ-9 severity bands

symptoms: Low mood, loss of interest or pleasure for at least 2 weeks.
Sleep or appetite change, tiredness, poor concentration, guilt or worthlessness.
Persistent excessive worry, restlessness, muscle tension, irritability (generalised anxiety).
Sudden attacks of intense fear with palpitations, breathlessness or dizziness (panic).
Fear of scrutiny in social situations (social anxiety).
Thoughts of death or of self-harm.
physicalSigns: Low or flat affect, slowed or agitated movement.
Tremor, sweating or fast heart rate from anxiety (look for thyroid or substance causes).
In children and adolescents irritability can replace low mood (MOH; outside the scope of this adult topic).
Self-neglect or poor weight gain or weight loss.
redFlags: Thoughts of suicide, a plan, intent or a recent attempt (PHQ-9 item 9 above zero): do not leave the patient alone; same-day senior clinician and psychiatry assessment (added clinical practice, see gaps).
Psychotic features (hallucinations, delusions) or acute severe suicidal ideation: MOH lists electroconvulsive therapy as first-line; refer to psychiatry urgently.
Past episode of mania or hypomania, or a family history of bipolar disorder: do not start an antidepressant alone; refer to psychiatry.
Severe functional collapse, refusal of food or fluids, or risk to others.
New confusion, fever, or abnormal vital signs: look for a medical cause (delirium, thyroid, sepsis, drug withdrawal) before labelling psychiatric.
precipitants: Previous depressive episodes or recurrence risk factors; extreme episodes including suicidality raise recurrence risk (MOH).
Female sex (higher prevalence in Saudi Arabia, MOH).
Substance, caffeine or alcohol use; medical illness; chronic pain.
Family history of mood or anxiety disorder.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Past mania or hypomania; antidepressant monotherapy may trigger mania; psychiatry referral.
Fatigue and low mood versus tremor, weight loss and palpitations; thyroid function test abnormal.
Caffeine, stimulants, alcohol, corticosteroids, withdrawal; history and timing.
Fluctuating attention, acute onset or progressive memory loss; older adult.

clinicalManagement.title: First minutes: safety
actions: Ask directly about thoughts of suicide or self-harm, a plan, intent and access to means; a positive answer (PHQ-9 item 9 above zero) means the patient stays with a staff member and a senior clinician and psychiatry see them the same day (added clinical practice; see gaps).
Check vital signs and glucose; exclude delirium, intoxication, withdrawal and a medical cause.
Ask about past mania or hypomania and psychosis before any antidepressant.

clinicalManagement.title: Screen
actions: Two-question screen: PHQ-2; a score of 3 or more leads to the full PHQ-9.
Anxiety: GAD-7; a score of 10 or more needs further evaluation.
Confirm with a diagnostic interview (DSM-5 or ICD-11); rule out thyroid disease, substances and comorbid depression or substance use.

clinicalManagement.title: Mild depression (PHQ-9 5 to 9, MOH mild tier)
actions: Non-drug options: psychoeducation, behavioural activation, problem solving, structured psychological support; repeat the PHQ-9 at follow-up (watchful waiting for mild scores).
Manage in primary care; refer to psychiatry if no improvement or risk emerges.

clinicalManagement.title: Moderate to severe depression (PHQ-9 10 or more)
actions: Start a first-line antidepressant (escitalopram 10 to 20 mg, fluoxetine 20 to 60 mg, duloxetine 60 mg, venlafaxine 75 to 225 mg, mirtazapine 15 to 45 mg, bupropion 150 to 300 mg, vortioxetine 10 to 20 mg, fluvoxamine 100 to 300 mg) plus psychological treatment (MOH).
Reassess tolerability and safety within 2 weeks; assess early improvement at 2 to 4 weeks; non-improvers who tolerate the drug have the dose increased, intolerant patients switch.
Severe (PHQ-9 20 or more): start medicine promptly and refer to psychiatry; psychotic features or acute suicidal ideation need psychiatry and electroconvulsive therapy is first-line.

clinicalManagement.title: Anxiety disorders
actions: Mild to moderate: cognitive behavioural therapy, medicine, or both. Severe: cognitive behavioural therapy plus medicine.
First-line medicines are SSRIs and SNRIs; start at half the usual starting dose because they can worsen anxiety at first (MOH).
Benzodiazepines only in a crisis, for 2 to 4 weeks at most (MOH).
Primary care manages mild cases; refer moderate to severe cases to psychiatry.

clinicalManagement.title: Inadequate response
actions: Reassess the diagnosis; check dose, duration and adherence; review comorbidity (depression, substance use).
Options: optimise the dose, add an adjunct (psychiatry), switch to another first-line or second-line agent, or move to a third-line agent.

clinicalManagement.title: Maintenance and stopping
actions: Depression: continue 6 to 9 months after remission, or 2 years or longer if recurrence risk factors are present (MOH).
Anxiety: treat for at least one year (MOH).
Taper rather than stopping suddenly (NHS venlafaxine page: over weeks to months).

regimens.indication: Major depressive disorder (first line); generalised anxiety, panic and social anxiety disorder (first line)
regimens.dose: 10 to 20 mg a day
regimens.duration: 6 to 9 months after remission (depression); at least 1 year (anxiety)
adjustments: First-line SSRI (MOH). NHS: low start, increase after a few weeks; several weeks to work. Renal and hepatic dose adjustment, pregnancy, breastfeeding, paediatric and older-adult dosing are not stated in either MOH protocol for this medicine; check the product information and pharmacy guide before prescribing in these groups.
MOH anxiety protocol: QTc-prolonging drugs are a relative contraindication; check the electrocardiogram when cardiac risk exists.
Pregnancy: NHS says use is allowed at the lowest effective dose after risk-benefit review.
monitoring: Tolerability and safety within 2 weeks; early response at 2 to 4 weeks; electrocardiogram if cardiac risk; suicidal thoughts.
contraindications: MOH lists none. NHS cautions: epilepsy, heart rhythm problems, heart disease, kidney or liver problems, bleeding disorder, glaucoma, past mania, MAO inhibitor use, interactions with anticoagulants, NSAIDs, St John's wort, and warning for suicidal thoughts.

medicationPlan.note: Dose ranges are from the MOH protocols; scoring, starting-dose and caution fill-ins are from NHS pages and the PHQ and GAD-7 instruments and are labelled. The MOH protocols give usual dose ranges only; they do not give starting doses, titration steps or maximum daily doses beyond the top of the range. Apart from the MOH anxiety statement to start at half the usual starting dose, the starting dose must come from the product information or hospital formulary. Renal and hepatic dose adjustment, pregnancy, breastfeeding, paediatric and older-adult dosing are not stated in either MOH protocol for this medicine; check the product information and pharmacy guide before prescribing in these groups. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Score of 3 or more out of 6: complete the full PHQ-9 (PHQ scoring summary, not MOH).
0 to 4 minimal; 5 to 9 mild; 10 to 14 moderate; 15 to 19 moderately severe; 20 to 27 severe (total range 0 to 27; each item scored 0 to 3).
0 to 4 minimal; 5 to 9 mild; 10 to 14 moderate; 15 to 21 severe (total range 0 to 21; each item scored 0 to 3); a score of 10 or more is the recommended cut-point for further evaluation.
Mild: non-drug options. Moderate to severe: medicine plus psychological treatment.
Mild to moderate: cognitive behavioural therapy, medicine, or both. Severe: both. Primary care manages mild disease; moderate to severe goes to psychiatry.

teaching.scope: Adult in primary care or the emergency room with low mood, worry, panic or unexplained physical symptoms: screening with the PHQ-2, PHQ-9 and GAD-7, immediate suicide-risk action, severity-based treatment (psychological, medicine, or both), antidepressant and anxiolytic choices with doses, review timings, referral to psychiatry and relapse prevention, using the Saudi Ministry of Health (MOH) major depressive disorder and anxiety disorders protocols. Scoring cut-offs, starting-dose gaps and safety cautions are filled from named international sources and labelled. Children, adolescents, bipolar disorder, psychosis and peripartum depression are outside this topic.
learningObjectives: Screen with PHQ-2, PHQ-9 and GAD-7, then confirm by diagnostic interview.
Ask about suicide every time and act the same day on a positive answer.
Match treatment to severity and reassess at 2 and 4 to 6 weeks.
pitfalls: Starting an antidepressant alone in possible bipolar disorder.
Missing thyroid disease or substance use.
Stopping a short half-life drug suddenly.
keyPoints: PHQ-2 of 3 or more leads to the PHQ-9; PHQ-9 of 10 or more is moderate.
GAD-7 of 10 or more needs further evaluation.
Continue antidepressants 6 to 9 months after remission; anxiety treatment at least a year.

patientEducation: Antidepressants take several weeks to work; take daily and do not stop suddenly.
Return or call urgently if thoughts of self-harm appear or worsen, especially in the first weeks and after dose changes.
lifestyleAndDiet: Regular sleep, physical activity, daylight and social contact.
Reduce caffeine; avoid alcohol and other substances.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician; psychiatry (Iradah Complex or MOH hospital psychiatric clinics); psychologist for cognitive behavioural therapy; clinical pharmacy; social work.
dischargeCriteria: Do not discharge a patient with active suicidal intent without psychiatry assessment; give written safety advice and a named follow-up.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review within 2 weeks for tolerability and safety, again at 2 to 4 weeks for early improvement, and at 4 to 8 weeks for response; repeat the PHQ-9 or GAD-7 at each visit.
